instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead, make the risotto. Grate 1/2 cup of the parmesan and set it aside. Pour 2 cups of the broth into a small saucepan and keep it hot over low heat.
Heat the 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium high. Add the 1 cup rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the grains look see-through at the edges and smell toasty.
Pour in the 1/4 cup wine. It'll hiss. Stir until it's soaked in, about 1 minute.

Add a ladle of the hot broth and stir until the rice has soaked up most of it. Keep adding the broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, until it's all in and the rice is tender with a little bite left in the middle, 18 to 20 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the 1/4 tsp salt and the parmesan. Spread the risotto out on a large plate and let it cool for 20 minutes.
Beat 1 of the eggs with a fork and stir it into the cooled rice. Cover it and put it in the fridge overnight, or for at least 3 hours, until it's cold and firm.
On the day, cut the 4 oz mozzarella into 8 cubes.
Set out three shallow bowls. Put the 1/4 cup flour in the first. Beat the other egg in the second. Put the 3/4 cup breadcrumbs in the third.

Wet your hands. Take an eighth of the rice, about 1/3 cup, and flatten it in your palm. Set a cube of mozzarella in the middle, close the rice around it and roll it into a ball. Pinch the seams shut. Any gap lets the cheese leak into the oil.
Roll each ball in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, pressing so the crumbs stick all over. Set them on a plate.

Pour the 3 cups vegetable oil into a heavy medium saucepan and heat it over medium. You're heating it to 350°F, so if you have a thermometer, clip it to the side. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of breadcrumbs. The oil is ready when they sizzle straight away and turn golden in about 30 seconds.
Meanwhile, warm 1 cup of the marinara in a small saucepan over low heat.

Fry 4 balls at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon, until they're deep golden all over. If they brown before 3 minutes, turn the heat down a little so the cheese has time to melt. Move them to a plate lined with paper towel.
Fry the other 4 the same way.
Serve them hot with the warm marinara on the side.
advance_prep_notes: make the risotto the night before, or at least 4 hours ahead, so it's cold and firm enough to roll
method_notes: All three cook the rice ahead, let it go completely cold, wrap it around a cube of mozzarella and fry the balls until golden. Christina's Cucina (the lead) makes a plain risotto with white wine and stock, stirs in an egg, chills it for hours or overnight, coats the balls in flour, egg and breadcrumbs, and serves them plain or with a little tomato sauce. GialloZafferano boils saffron rice with butter and caciocavallo and fills half with ragù and half with ham and mozzarella, and Taste of Home stirs Parmesan and an egg yolk into saffron rice and coats the balls in egg white. This one follows the lead and adds Parmesan to the rice.

sources.name: Christina's Cucina
sources.title: Arancini di Riso: Sicilian Rice Balls
